printed_hypotheses: K binomial;R an augmented K-lambda-algebra;N in R with lambda^k(N)=0 for k>d;x in Fil^i R. No epsilon(N)=d condition is stated.

example.ring: K=Z,R=Z[L,L^-1],epsilon(L)=1. Define lambda_t(sum_j m_jL^j)=product_j(1+L^jt)^m_j for finite integer coefficient families. These are the line-element lambda operations;the universal lambda identities follow by substitution of the line powers and extension to additive inverses through reciprocals of formal series.
example.augmentation_map: epsilon:R→Z sends each L^j to1,and sends the displayed total lambda series to(1+t)^(sum_j m_j),so it commutes with every lambda coefficient.
example.data: N=0,d=1,i=1,x=L-1. All lambda^k(N) with k>=1 vanish;epsilon(x)=0 so x is in Fil^1.
example.modified_operation: D=lambda_(-1)(0)=1. The defining identity gamma^p(N,x)D=gamma^p(xD) therefore gives gamma^p(0,x)=gamma^p(x).

exact_filtration.containment: Every augmentation-zero element z has the expression sum_j m_j(L^j-1). Each L^j-1 lies in I,also for negative j. The product gamma_t(z)=product_j(1+(L^j-1)t)^m_j shows gamma^r(z) in I^r. Every canonical-filtration generator of total index at least q therefore lies in I^q.
exact_filtration.reverse_containment: x=L-1 has augmentation zero,and gamma^1(x)^q=x^q is a defining generator of Fil^q. Since Fil^q is an ideal,it contains I^q.
exact_filtration.separating_map: h:R→Z[u]/(u^2) sends L to1+u,L^-1 to1-u. It is a well-defined ring map because(1+u)(1-u)=1. It kills I^2=Fil^2 and sends the asserted difference x to nonzero u.
